title: feat(post): waterjet records, CR LF, travel, programBounds and a generic waterjet post
body:
## Latest review follow-up: reserved pockets and the arc guard

Final head: `fd9e31b9fd6d46be6b31acb6447d98c771b67978`.
The fix commit is `c6a612de3`. The head also merges upstream main `ddc4d8274` (two merges of main, no conflict, no hand edit).

This update fixes the two findings of the review of `9d5db9bec`.

1. The combined tree compiles again. `reservations::check_stream` (main's #3284) now has the two new records.
   - `Record::Jet(_)` is in the arm that has `Record::Torch(_)`. A jet is cutting: it needs a stated TOOL, and it obeys a reserved pocket.
   - `Record::Waterjet(_)` is in the arm that has `Record::Plasma(_)`. The header is no motion.
   - Pin: `a_waterjet_stream_obeys_the_reserved_pockets` (`crates/post/tests/tool_reservations.rs`). The machine is `kind: waterjet` and states `tooling.reserved`.
2. The post no longer writes a short arc as a full-circle block. `onCircular` of `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` reads `arcFate(arcWord, arcIncOf(fu))`, as `tormach-plasma.cps` does.
   - On `"linear"` it calls `onLinear()`. On `"none"` it writes no block.
   - The reviewer's stream now posts `G1 X59.5 Y30 F300` then `G1 X70 Y30`, with no `G3` block and no warning.
   - Pins:
     - `every_post_writes_no_coincident_arc_block_and_keeps_its_real_arcs` (`coincident_arcs.rs`): `waterjet-iso` is in the `POSTS` table, with a flat witness that has the `WATERJET` header and a `JET ON` span.
     - `waterjet_post_writes_no_full_circle_for_an_arc_under_the_output_step` (`waterjet_iso_post.rs`): the reviewer's stream, mm and inch.
     - `waterjet_post_writes_a_same_angle_arc_as_its_straight_move` (`waterjet_iso_post.rs`): the #3474 witnesses and the #3500 offset-centre witnesses, mm and inch, and one normal quarter arc that stays `G3 X10 Y15 I-10 J0`.

Pin proof (mutation checks, each restored to GREEN):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| The `arcFate` branch removed from `onCircular` | RED: the `coincident_arcs` table test and the two new `waterjet_iso_post` tests fail |
| `Record::Jet(_)` moved to the no-motion arm | RED: `a_waterjet_stream_obeys_the_reserved_pockets` fails |
| `Record::Waterjet(_)` moved to the motion arm | RED: the same test fails (`TOOL selector is not stated` for a header before TOOL) |
| The two match arms removed (the reviewed head with main) | RED: `camcraft-post` does not compile (`E0004`) |

Results on the final head `fd9e31b9f`, against upstream main `ddc4d8274`, Linux, `rustc 1.100.0`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 1,169 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled; 23.9 minutes. The failed step is `ui suites: egui_app`: `killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV)`, no failed test |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only "ui suites: egui_app"` | GREEN (the step alone, one run) |
| `clippy -D warnings` (gate step) | GREEN |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | passed (gate steps) |
| `app suites: first_router_part` | passed (main's #3703 is in this head) |
| `post suites: coincident_arcs`, `same_angle_arcs`, `tool_reservations`, `tool_reservations_cli`, `waterjet_iso_post`, `script_waterjet_iso`, `waterjet_engine` | passed |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | GREEN: 3 steps, 0 failed |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | GREEN: 257 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 42.8 minutes |

The `egui_app` crash agrees with the open #3605 class of the earlier rounds (a GPU device in a test process). This PR changes no file in `crates/ui` or `crates/gpu`.

Goldens moved in this round: none. `waterjet_iso_post` (the `plate.nc` and `plate_inch_chords.nc` goldens) and `script_waterjet_iso` (11 refusal goldens) ran and pass with no regeneration. The catalog suites ran and pass.

Not exercised in this round:

- The full quick gate did not run a second time after the `egui_app` crash. Only that step ran again.
- Upstream main moved to `2de071415` (#3656, motion) after the gates. A trial merge with it (`git merge-tree`) is clean. The gates did not run on that tree.
- No pixel snapshot ran. There is no UI change, so no screenshots apply.

Note, not changed here: `programBounds` boxes a short arc record by its full circle (`machine::move_extremes`). The `(EXTENT ...)` comment and the travel check are thus on the safe side for such a record. The new pins compare the blocks without that comment.

The PR remains a draft. The labels are unchanged. The sections below describe earlier rounds.

## Earlier round: required checks green on the combined tree

Head of that round: `9d5db9bec970f4bc84ba682a6a9e6d53f0399a9a`.
This head is a merge of upstream main `f2b2369edb69e73b464b401d979f2e134751542a` into `e302dc0f0`.
The merge had no conflict and no hand edit. `git show --remerge-diff` is empty. No source file of this PR changed.

The review of `e302dc0f0` asked for two green required checks. Both are green on this head.
The run used a Linux host with a usable graphics adapter and `rustc 1.100.0`.

1. Graphics-dependent UI result: GREEN. `ui suites: lib`, `ui suites: egui_app` and `ui suites: shell` pass in the quick gate. `headless_run_succeeds` passes.
2. Clippy on the combined tree: GREEN. The gate step ran `cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`. `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs` is not changed. `rustc 1.100.0` does not report `needless_range_loop` there.

Results on the final head:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | GREEN: 1,149 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 49.8 minutes |
| Clippy (gate step, nine crates, `--all-targets -- -D warnings`) | GREEN |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | passed (gate steps) |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | GREEN: 255 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 40.8 minutes |

Not green before the merge, on `e302dc0f0`, on the same host:

- Two full quick gate runs were RED: 1,131 steps each. Run 1 had 2 failed steps: `ui suites: lib` and `ui suites: trace_parity`. Run 2 had 1 failed step: `ui suites: trace_parity`. Each failure was `killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV)` with no failed test and no panic text.
- The two steps passed when they ran alone. `ui suites: trace_parity` passed 4 of 4 times alone.
- These crashes agree with #3589 (fixed on main by PR #3604, in this merge) and with the open #3605 (`trace_parity` makes a GPU device in each test with no lock). This PR changes no file in `crates/ui` or `crates/gpu`.
- `ui suites: trace_parity` passed in the one full run on the final head. #3605 is open, so the crash can come back at intervals.

Not exercised in this round:

- The light lane did not run. The reviewer's light run on `e302dc0f0` was GREEN.
- No pixel snapshot ran.
- The checks did not run on macOS or with `rustc 1.99.1`.
- Upstream main moved to `82db54282` after the gates. A trial merge with it (`git merge-tree`) is clean. The gates did not run on that tree.

No source fix was made in this round, so no new pin or mutation check applies. No program or golden changed. There is no UI change, so no screenshots apply.
The PR remains a draft. The labels are unchanged. The results below describe earlier rounds.

## Review fixes and final-head validation

Head of that round: `e302dc0f000ecde4f2a52ddb63fb9879b6004f5a`.

This update fixes the three findings of the review of `05243edc5`.

1. A section with no `WATERJET` header after a waterjet section is refused by name.
   - The engine now sets the section's current properties before `onSection`. The hook no longer reads a header that the previous `ENDSECTION` cleared.
   - The post refuses a jet word or a cut with no header in `jetOk` (new `headerOk`). It never drops the motion without a warning.
   - Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_an_adjacent_section_with_no_header` (the review's input). The test checks the named refusal, the first section's `G1 X1 Y0 F300`, one nozzle comment and one `G54`.
2. Merge of upstream main `35940da16`. Conflicts resolved:
   - `engine.rs`: main's upright-after-tilt refusal and `machine::flatten` stay. `programBounds` is published after `set_machine`.
   - `mod.rs`: `machine_installation` and `machine_travel` both stay.
   - `comment_escape.rs`: main's native-Agie refusal check stays. The waterjet machine kind stays. The count is now `text_posts == 22` (23 shipped posts, 1 native refusal).
3. Quick gate on the final combined head: GREEN (below).

Mutation checks on pin 1:

- Engine refresh removed: RED (two nozzle comments).
- Engine refresh and post `headerOk` guard both removed: RED (no warning, the review's silent output).
- Both restored: GREEN.
- The post guard alone is a second guard. With the engine refresh in place, `startPreamble` refuses first, so the pin cannot isolate the post guard.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 1,131 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 20.4 minutes.
- Clippy (gate step, `-p` all nine selected crates, `--all-targets -- -D warnings`): GREEN.
- `adaptive_troch_parallel`: passed in 16 s in the gate. The earlier 90 s timing failure did not repeat.
- `comment_escape`, `waterjet_engine`, `waterjet_iso_post`, `script_waterjet_iso`: pass on the merged tree.
- The heavy lanes and the light lane did not run in this round. The reviewer's heavy run on `05243edc5` was GREEN.

The PR remains a draft. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

The sections below describe the original implementation and its historical validation. Their test counts and gate results are historical.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 996 steps, 0 failed (wall 30.5 min; the `cl` change reaches each dependent crate). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branch history: the first commit was squashed onto a newer main by mistake, so it reverted nine files of the Tormach lathe G76 work (#2952). The second commit restores them from main. The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

## Goldens moved

None. All goldens are new: `crates/post/tests/golden/waterjet/plate.nc`, `plate_inch_chords.nc` and the input `plate.cnc`, plus `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/waterjet-iso/*.refusal`. No existing `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.

## Not exercised

- No generator writes the waterjet records yet. The `Toolpath::waterjet` field and its `.cl` dump come with the WaterjetProfile operation (#1883). The input stream here is written by hand.
- The post is not in `posting::BUILTINS`, so the app does not offer it yet (see the decision record). A user can post with it as a file of their own (`serves = ["waterjet"]`).
- The post did not run on a real waterjet control.

## Overlaps

- #3037 changes `engine.rs` (the `Script::load` line in `run_program_with`) and `js.rs`. This PR touches the same file, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2893 changes `engine.rs` and `js.rs` (fine boring). Same file, different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Post: generic ISO abrasive-waterjet post (`waterjet-iso.cps`), WATERJET / JET stream records with `onJetOn` / `onJetOff`, CR LF output (`lineEnding`), `machine.travel`, `programBounds` and arc linearization (`linearizeArcs`) for scripts.

Effort: high

Fixes #1882
